title: FoodData Central: Foundation Foods
publisher: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service
citation: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service. FoodData Central: Foundation Foods. fdc.nal.usda.gov
version: rolling releases; see publication date per food in FoodData Central
selection: 30 of 424 Foundation Foods, picked at random (seed 42) with at most one food per distinct first part of the name (the text before the first comma or bracket)

title: NEVO online 2025/9.0, with LanguaL and FoodEx2
publisher: National Institute for Public Health and the Environment (RIVM)
selection: 30 foods from the NEVO online 2025/9.0 LanguaL and FoodEx2 table (2,328 foods). A food was eligible when its FoodEx2 code reads as one code (base term, then optional facets) and does not use the ingredient facet F04, and its Dutch name does not contain: the word gem; schotel, soep, salade, pizza, nasi, bami, stamppot, kant-en-klaar or huishoudelijk bereid; a lone m, z, v or p; obv, excl, incl, hoh, vetz, KH, ea or multivit; opvolgmelk, zuigelingenvoeding, kindervoeding, babyvoeding or peuter; a slash; or a brand token (AH, Albert, Heijn, Jumbo, Etos, Kruidvat, Becel, Nutrilon, Kellogg, Nestle, Liga, Hero, Nutrasense, Bonbebe, Roosvicee, Modifast, Yakult, Activia, Hipp, Olvarit, Nutricia, Taksi, Karvan, Cevitam, Bolletje, Ovomaltine, Nibb-it, Wokkels, Krispies, Isostar, Campina, Unox, Knorr, Maggi, Calve, Iglo, Optimel, Alpro, Quaker, Lipton, LoSalt, Capri-Sun, All-Bran, ERU, LU, Knijpfruit, Slurpfruit, M&M, Campari, Bugles, AA-Drink). Sorted by NEVO-code, shuffled with Python 3.11 random.Random(42), then the first 30 with a different first word. Mentos was not on the brand list; it was dropped because the name is only a brand, and replaced by the next food from that draw, Ui sla- rauw.

title: The food classification and description system FoodEx2 (revision 2)
citation: European Food Safety Authority, 2015. The food classification and description system FoodEx2 (revision 2). EFSA supporting publication 2015:EN-804. 90 pp.
selection: The worked encoding examples in chapter 5 (sections 5.1.4 to 5.13). Each row is a food the guidance codes, with the FoodEx2 code it assigns. Lists of food groups, and codes shown only to explain syntax, are not included.

title: McCance and Widdowson’s The Composition of Foods Integrated Dataset 2021
citation: Public Health England. McCance and Widdowson’s The Composition of Foods Integrated Dataset 2021. London: Public Health England, 2021.
selection: 30 of 2,887 foods on the Factors worksheet of the 2021 workbook. Ordered by Food Code, shuffled with Python 3.11 random.Random(42), then the first 30 with a different first part of the name (the text before the first comma, or the whole name when there is no comma), compared without regard to capitals. The data file lists them alphabetically by food name. Food code 13-669 is printed twice in the workbook (aubergine roasted in rapeseed oil, and watercress, raw); neither was drawn.
